name: Dominica
summary: Dominica taxes resident individuals on worldwide income at up to 35% (above XCD 80,000 including the XCD 30,000 allowance), so foreign dividends and interest are taxed, with a unilateral foreign tax credit. There is no capital gains, inheritance, estate or wealth tax. Domestic dividends carry a dividend tax credit that largely removes the tax. Residents who are not ordinarily resident are taxed on foreign income only when received in Dominica. Citizenship by investment from USD 200,000.

regimes.name: Resident
regimes.description: Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income; no capital gains tax.
regimes.eligibility: Physically present at least 183 days in the year (Deloitte; IRD), or otherwise resident under the Income Tax Act definition.

capital_gains.rate_basis: No capital gains tax (Deloitte 2026; CBIU). Income Tax Act s.33 taxes 'gains or profits' of a business and a residual category; capital gains of an investor are not charged.

capital_gains.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on transfers of immovable property: 2.5% paid by the seller and 2% by the buyer (also on sales of shares in companies with more than 50% real property). Additional fees may apply: assurance fund 1%, judicial fee 1%, solicitor's fee up to 2.5% plus 15% VAT. Non-citizens need an alien landholding licence (cost not verified).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains of a business (e.g. dealing in securities) are business income at up to 35%.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Dominican companies are included in income but carry a tax credit (s.63): full credit where the marginal rate is 30% or less, otherwise 35% of the net dividend, so domestic dividends are effectively untaxed. Foreign dividends are taxed at up to 35% with credit for foreign tax (lesser of foreign tax and Dominica tax).
dividends.rate_basis: Bands after the XCD 30,000 resident allowance: 15% next 20,000, 25% next 30,000, 35% above XCD 80,000 (IRD, from 1 January 2018). Domestic: s.63(2) credit offsets the tax. Foreign: top rate 0.35.

dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% on dividends to non-residents; no WHT on dividends to residents.
dividends.treaty_network: Only the CARICOM multilateral treaty. No US or EU treaties, so foreign WHT on the portfolio is not reduced; it is creditable unilaterally (ss.64-65).
dividends.important_exceptions: Resident but not ordinarily resident individuals: foreign-source income is taxed only to the extent received in Dominica (s.8(2)).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No national property tax; municipal tax paid to city and village councils.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. Transfers of property by gift may bear transfer taxes and fees.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. A parent transferring property to a child pays 2% stamp duty on its value; assurance fund (1%) and judicial (1%) fees may also apply (Deloitte 2026).

open_questions: Stamp duty and fees when land passes on death.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident: present 183 days or more in the year (Deloitte; IRD); the Act also treats as resident a person present for a continuous period spanning adjacent years. 'Ordinarily resident' individuals are taxed on worldwide income; residents not ordinarily resident only on foreign income received in Dominica.

routes.name: Citizenship by investment: Economic Diversification Fund
routes.requirements: Non-refundable USD 200,000 single applicant; USD 250,000 for a main applicant plus up to 3 dependants; USD 25,000 per extra dependant under 18, USD 40,000 per extra dependant 18+. Fees: processing USD 1,000, due diligence USD 7,500 main + USD 4,000 per dependant 16+, naturalisation USD 500 each, interview USD 1,000. Applications only through authorised agents (CBI Regulations 2024).

routes.name: Citizenship by investment: approved real estate
routes.requirements: USD 200,000 in an approved project, held 3 years (5 if resold to another CBI applicant); government fee USD 100,000 for main applicant + up to 3 dependants.

corporate.summary: Corporate income tax 25%; branch remittance tax 15%; no CGT; unilateral foreign tax credit; no Pillar Two commitment. 15% WHT on dividends, interest and royalties to non-residents.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median of the three priced family houses on Caribbean Paradise Realty's Dominica 'furnished, US$3,000 and up' long-term rental page on 15 Oct 2026: a 4-bedroom, 4.5-bath ocean-view house in Morne Daniel USD 8,000 (tenant pays electricity); a 3-bedroom house with pool near Roseau USD 4,000 (main house; a 1-bedroom lower apartment can be added); a 3-bedroom house with a separate 1-bedroom apartment in Morne Daniel USD 3,500. Only one is a true 4-bedroom house; the other two reach 4 bedrooms only with their annex apartments. Listings undated. Small sample. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

source.title: Caribbean Paradise Realty: Dominica long-term rentals, furnished US$3,000 and up

cost_of_living.notes: International school fee not sourced: no private or international secondary school in Dominica publishes a fee schedule online (re-checked 15 Oct 2026). Purchase price per m2, health insurance and housekeeper not sourced.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens are taxed by the US on worldwide income; Dominica tax on foreign dividends may be creditable in the US. No US-Dominica treaty.
open_questions: 2025-2026 CBI changes (regional Eastern Caribbean regulator, harmonised USD 200,000 minimum) not verified on an official page; CBIU news lists no price change in July-September 2026.
Precise meaning of 'ordinarily resident' for a newly arrived family (definition partly illegible in the scanned Act).

Private/international secondary school fee for Dominica not sourced: re-checked 15 Oct 2026 including third-party listings (International Schools Database, expat guides): no dated fee schedule for a Dominica private secondary school is published; undated expat-guide ranges were not used. The household cost metric lacks the school component until one is obtained from a school.
